project: Property Abundance — cash home buying ad

derived_from.shot_grammar: Measured from 10_Video_Builds/Ad5_Skeptic_v1/PropertyAbundance_Ad5_Skeptic_v2_REAL.mp4 — 1080x1920, 30 fps, 32.760 s, 9 shots, lengths 2.93 / 9.80 / 4.83 / 1.70 / 2.67 / 1.13 / 1.70 / 5.50 / 2.49 s. Grammar borrowed, topic and cast NOT copied.
derived_from.hooks: 05_Tutorials/Hook_Psychology_Research_Report.md — 'Key takeaways: the hook playbook' and the Loop order rule.

output_spec.audio: native voiceover, no music from the model

SHOT_RHYTHM_RULE.why: Uniform shot lengths read as a slideshow. The reference varies from 1.13 s to 9.80 s.
SHOT_RHYTHM_RULE.required_pattern: Never two consecutive shots of the same length or the same framing. Every clip must contain at least one shot under 1.6 s and at least one shot over 4 s.
SHOT_RHYTHM_RULE.framing_ladder: Rotate through: extreme close-up on an object, wide establishing, over-the-shoulder, low angle, top-down, mid on a person. Never repeat the previous shot's framing.
SHOT_RHYTHM_RULE.presenter_rule: The presenter appears in at most ONE shot per clip. Every other shot is b-roll of the thing being spoken about.
SHOT_RHYTHM_RULE.show_the_noun: Whatever noun the voiceover says, that object fills the frame. Repairs means a roofer. Waiting means an unopened letter. Never a person describing a thing.

style_lock.render_style: non-photorealistic stylized 3D animation, like a modern animated feature film
stylization_anchors: matte painted surfaces with no glossy specular highlights
flat clean skin shading with no pore, wrinkle or stubble detail
hair as a single sculpted shape, not individual strands
cloth as smooth simplified folds, not simulated weave
must_not_look_like: realistic skin pores or subsurface scattering
style_lock.drift_guard: If any frame starts to read as a real human or as live action, push further toward the animated feature look. Stylized always wins over realistic.
style_lock.palette: muted cream, warm grey, soft navy, one amber accent

character_lock.identity: one man, Black American, early forties, medium-brown skin, close-cropped hair, short trimmed beard with a few greys at the chin, calm and direct, an ordinary neighbour and not a model
character_lock.wardrobe: navy henley, sleeves pushed up below the elbow, no logo, no collar, mid-grey trousers
character_lock.wardrobe_lock: identical in every shot he appears in. No polo, no white shirt, no jacket, no change of clothing.
character_lock.role_lock: buyer-side host who explains what the company does. NEVER a past customer, never a seller, never a testimonial.
character_lock.screen_time: he appears in three shots across the whole ad. Everything else is b-roll.

global_negative: no written text of any kind anywhere in the picture
no numbers, digits, prices, percentages or currency symbols rendered in frame
no measurements, dimension labels, arrows or diagram markings
no letters, words, handwriting, printing or signatures
no captions, subtitles, titles or lower thirds
no logos, brand marks or watermarks
no cash, banknotes, coins or money counters
no dissolves, wipes or fades — hard cuts only
no music, no whoosh, no sting on any cut
do not ask questions, do not request a reference image

loop_design.pattern: nested, per the Loop order rule — Open A, Open B, Close B, Close A. Nothing opens and closes back to back.

loop_A.closes: L8, the last line before the CTA
loop_A.payload: the biggest promise, saved for the final close

loop_B.note: closed while A is still open

spoken_lines_manifest.note: Eight lines, each spoken exactly once. Numbers are NEVER spoken — they appear only as caption cards you burn in editing.

lines.text: Don't list your house until you've seen this number.
Not the offer. What you actually keep.
Start with what it's worth fixed up.
Then take out the roof, the furnace, the kitchen.
Then the commission, and every month it sits.
That's the number they never put on screen.
We take the house as it stands.
And we hand you the sheet we worked it out on.

shots.action: one more envelope drops onto the stack and settles

speech.text: Don't list your house until you've seen this number.

shots.sound: a light paper slap as the envelope lands, quiet hallway room tone

shots.framing: wide establishing, low angle from the sidewalk looking up at a single-storey cream house set back behind a mown lawn, a bare young tree at frame left
shots.action: an empty front porch, nothing moves but leaves on the young tree

speech.text: Start with what it's worth fixed up.

shots.framing: over-the-shoulder from behind the man, looking past him up the concrete path to the plain front door of the cream house

speech.text: We take the house as it stands.

persistent_hook_banner.text: DON'T LIST UNTIL YOU'VE SEEN THIS NUMBER
persistent_hook_banner.position: pinned top of frame for the entire 33 seconds, never leaves
persistent_hook_banner.style: black box, amber outline, white all-caps

post_production_by_you.word_captions: word-by-word at the bottom, white all-caps, one keyword per phrase in amber

number_cards.rule: Numbers are NEVER spoken and NEVER generated. They are burned over the b-roll beds marked caption_bed_note.
number_cards.compliance: Every number card carries a small amber EXAMPLE badge, exactly as the reference does. The figures must come from Property Abundance's real offer worksheet. Do not ship invented figures even with the badge.

post_production_by_you.end_card: Over the empty sky in the final shot: Property Abundance name, logo, form URL. Every visible word in this ad is burned here. The model has failed to render legible text three times and must never be asked for it.
post_production_by_you.audio: Normalise the joined file to -14 LUFS integrated, -1.5 dBTP.

must_be_true_before_this_runs: L7 'We take the house as it stands' — no repair, cleaning or clear-out requirement, ever.
L8 'we hand you the sheet we worked it out on' — a real offer worksheet exists and is given to the seller.
Every number card — figures come from that real worksheet. The EXAMPLE badge labels a worked example, it does not license an invented one.
The host is a spokesperson for the company, never a past customer. FTC 16 CFR 255.1 and 16 CFR 465.2.
